notes: Agent hook journeys. These cover hooks as an agent capability -- whether a declared hook runs and what its output reaches -- rather than the listing that shows them, which is a panel and lives with the panels. The effect a user depends on is asserted through the request body, by scripting a turn that only answers when the hook's stdout is present and pairing it with a turn that answers when it is not.

scenarios.name: A per-prompt hook's output is in the request the model receives
scenarios.description: A userPromptSubmit hook that prints a sentinel -- asserts the sentinel is present in the request body the agent sends, which is the only place a context hook's effect can be observed
steps: prompt:answer once the prompt hook has run
scenarios.observe: A context hook exists to put something in front of the model, and no panel can show whether it did. The answering turn is matched on the request body containing the hook's stdout, so it can only fire if the hook ran and its output was injected; the paired turn answers whenever that is missing, which turns a silently dropped hook into a named string on screen instead of a timeout. The sentinel is arithmetic the shell resolves, so the matched literal exists nowhere in the agent config that declares the hook -- only in what the hook printed. Asserting the second absent is what makes the first meaningful.

scenarios.name: A pre-tool hook that refuses stops the tool from running
scenarios.description: A preToolUse hook matched to the file-read tool that exits non-zero -- asserts the tool is reported as failed rather than executed, and the turn continues afterwards
scenarios.observe: A pre-tool hook is the one hook that can stop an action, and this pins that it does: the call is reported failed and the model still gets its turn, so a refusal neither runs the tool nor wedges the session. The refusal also preempts the approval gate entirely -- this same read asks for approval when the matcher does not name it, and here no gate ever appears, so the hook is consulted before the user is. Known gap this deliberately does not assert: the hook's own stderr never reaches the screen, so the card says only 'Tool execution failed' and a user cannot see which hook refused or why. Asserting the reason would fail today; asserting its absence would fail once it is surfaced.

scenarios.name: A pre-tool hook matched to another tool leaves this one alone
scenarios.description: The same refusing preToolUse hook, matched to a tool the turn never calls -- asserts the call it does make runs normally, so the refusal is scoped by the matcher rather than applied to everything
steps: prompt:read the manifest with a scoped hook
scenarios.observe: This is the control for the refusal journey, and without it a hook engine that refused every tool would pass that one. The hook is identical and still exits non-zero; only its matcher differs, naming a tool this turn never calls. The read therefore reaches its approval gate and completes once approved, which the absent failure text checks -- the same string the refusal journey asserts present, so the two together attribute the outcome to the matcher rather than to the hook merely existing. That the gate appears at all is the other half: a refused call never reaches it.

match.userInputContains: read the manifest with a scoped hook
